column1: # Build 6 -- half-width SANDWICHED, with original text on BOTH sides.
# Build 5 overturned the previous conclusion: "ENGLISH TAIL" rendered on
# screen, in a dialogue block, at correct half-width metrics. Dialogue does
# NOT reject half-width. What it does is re-wrap and truncate around it.
# Build 5 in detail:
#   AROUND  line1 = 6 JP + 7 EN, line2 = 9 JP (untouched)
#           drew  row1 = 6 JP   row2 = 7 EN + the first 2 cells of line 2
#           the last 7 cells of line 2 never appeared
#   BARKEEP one line, 8 JP + 4 EN -> drew the 8 JP only, no second row
# So the first half-width word behaves like a line break, and everything
# after it slides up into the next row and gets clipped at the block's line
# count. A line that BEGINS with half-width therefore reports zero cells,
# which is why builds 2-4 produced no window at all rather than a broken one.
# This build puts original glyphs AFTER the English too, to separate
# "acts as a line break, rendering continues" from "stops there".
# offset  keep  text     (text no longer has to fill the line)
# BARKEEP, one line of 12 cells: 4 JP, 4 EN, 4 JP.
#   4 JP only              -> hard stop at the half-width word
#   4 JP + 4 EN + 4 JP     -> mid-line half-width is harmless, and the
#                             earlier failures were about the line HEAD
#   4 JP then a new row    -> line break, and a 1-line block clips the rest
# AROUND: line 1 left ENTIRELY original. English goes mid-way into LINE 2
# only. If row 1 comes out as the full 13-cell Japanese, the damage is local
# to the line that contains half-width, which is the best case available.
